title: Hypothesis-led A/B & Multivariate Split Composer with Statistical Guidance
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design a guided composer for creating hypothesis-driven A/B and multivariate traffic splits inside Redwood Console. The composer should surface sample-size/power guidance, adaptive stopping recommendations, and clear visualizations of confidence intervals and uplift for primary metrics. The goal is to reduce common setup errors, encourage pre-registered hypotheses, and make rollbacks and fallbacks explicit in the flow.
goals: Help engineers and product managers set up statistically sound experiments without leaving the Console
Make sample size, expected duration, and statistical power visible and actionable
Tie rollout safety gates to experiment thresholds and automatic rollback policies
Support simple multivariate splits (up to 4 variants) with option to convert to canary or staged rollout
out_of_scope: Auto-aggregation of third-party metric sources (will accept Datadog/Prometheus links in v2)
summary_of_work: Initial concept (2026-02-10): wireframes showing hypothesis input, metric selection, traffic allocation, and power/margin estimates
Iterated on metric UX (2026-02-22): added primary/secondary metric toggle and inline examples for common ML/infra metrics
Prototype built (2026-03-01): interactive Figma flow that calculates sample size estimates from baseline rate + minimum detectable effect
Design review with PM/Eng (2026-03-05): agreed on MVP statistical model (frequentist two-sample test) and server-side calculation approach
Accessibility pass (2026-03-09): color contrast and keyboard flow validated for the key visualizations
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Implement frequentist power calculations for MVP rather than Bayesian credible intervals to reduce backend complexity and match most users' expectations
Trade-off: Sample size estimator will assume independence and stable baseline; we will surface assumptions clearly in the UI and link to a detailed guide
Decision: Limit multivariate composer to 4 variants in MVP to keep visualization and sample-size guidance comprehensible
Trade-off: Heavy statistical computation will run server-side (not in client) to avoid exposing slow calculation on low-end machines; requires new lightweight API endpoint
open_issues: How to handle metric sources that are only available post-deployment (we propose a 'deferred metric' flag)
Rollout integration: should experiment state map directly to canary policies or remain as separate artifact? (PM prefers unified flow)
Edge-case: small-traffic customers where required sample size exceeds feasible duration — need templated recommendations
accessibility: Charts use high-contrast palettes with pattern fills for colorblind users
All interactive controls have keyboard focus states and aria labels in the prototype
Numeric inputs validate and provide inline helper text for confidence level and MDE (minimum detectable effect)
feedback_and_reviews: PM feedback (Mar 5) - Diego Ramirez: Narrow MVP to a single primary metric and add 'fast-fail' checkbox for automatic rollback if metric drops > X%
Eng feedback (Mar 5) - Priya Malhotra: Backend should expose a /power-estimate endpoint; keep client-side only for rendering; suggested caching for repeated calls
Design review (Mar 9) - Marcus Lee: Replace stacked bar with interval plot to better show confidence bands and overlapping CIs
UX research (Mar 11) - Notes from 6 moderated sessions: users liked pre-flight checks and disclaimers; they were confused by 'sequential testing' language — changed to 'adaptive stopping'
